text:
sam_support: Customer reports intermittent 502s to our hosted API through their AWS PrivateLink setup. They see DNS responses rotate between two private IPs and occasional TLS handshake failures (certificate name mismatch). They provided traces and asked for repro help.
lee_infra: Can you drop the dig(+short) and curl -v outputs they captured? Also any route table / VPCE config screenshots?
sam_support: Paste from customer: 
```
$ dig api.redwood.example +short
10.0.2.45
10.0.2.46
```
and curl -v to 10.0.2.45 sometimes shows: 
```
* TLS handshake: alert handshake_failure
* Server certificate: subject CN=lb.internal.redwood
```
kyla_ops: Quick thought — split-horizon / PHZ + VPCE private DNS misconfig can cause some queries to resolve to a public ALB IP (or an internal ALB with a different cert). Are they chaining interface endpoint -> NLB -> ALB by chance? :thinking_face:
lee_infra: If there's an NLB in front of an ALB and TLS is terminated at the ALB, IP rotation without consistent SNI per connection can hit an endpoint with a different cert. Also check endpoint policy and target group health.
hema: Ask them to run explicit checks against each returned IP and capture ClientHello SNI. Example commands to repro on their side: 
```
# force-resolve to a single IP
curl --resolve api.redwood.example:443:10.0.2.45 -v https://api.redwood.example/health
# sni and cert check
openssl s_client -servername api.redwood.example -connect 10.0.2.45:443 -showcerts
# check resolver behaviour
dig +short api.redwood.example @169.254.169.253
```
sam_support: Customer ran similar checks. They observed TTLs fluctuating: TTL=60 then TTL=1 then back to 60 over ~30s. Their outbound proxy does round-robin across the IPs and does not set SNI per connection (single upstream connection reused). They also have an egress allowlist that only permits one of the IP ranges initially returned.
lee_infra: That fits intermittent TLS name mismatches — proxy picks an IP that presents internal cert, so handshake fails. Two likely root causes: (1) misconfiguration on one backend (ALB/NLB) serving wrong cert, (2) VPCE private DNS sometimes resolving to a different zone (public vs private) due to PHZ/resolver fallback.
kyla_ops: Also confirm VPC endpoint private DNS checkbox and Route53 association(s). If the PHZ association is partial or there's a public zone with same name in another account, some queries may go to the public resolver. Check resolver rules, conditional forwarders, and any on-prem DNS forwarders for EDNS/cache behavior.
lee_infra: I'll check our side first: target groups, cert bundles, and recent ALB/ingress canary deploys in us-east-1. If one instance accidentally got an internal cert CN=lb.internal.redwood, that'll explain cert mismatch.
ops-bot: monitor: 502 spike detected in us-east-1 (15:12–15:18) +18% error rate.
sam_support: Customer also attached SG/NACL screenshots — ephemeral ports are allowed, but their proxy has a very short connection reuse timeout which amplifies rotation. They also confirmed they see differing certificates when hitting the two IPs directly via openssl s_client: 10.0.2.46 -> CN=api.redwood.example (OK), 10.0.2.45 -> CN=lb.internal.redwood (mismatch).
hema: Action items: 
- lee_infra: roll back the ALB/ingress canary in us-east-1 to the previous config and verify certs.
- infra: verify VPCE private DNS associations and ensure no public-zone fallback for api.redwood.example PHZ.
- sam_support: ask customer to temporarily pin to the good IP or update proxy to set SNI per connection and allow both cert CNs during the incident.
lee_infra: Starting rollback of canary now, posting progress.
lee_infra: rollback complete, removed the bad canary change. Re-running internal probes.
ops-bot: monitor: 502s back to baseline, spike resolved.
sam_support: Customer reports API 200 responses restored. They confirmed TLS handshakes now succeed consistently. I'll close the support ticket after we validate DNS TTL/PHZ settings with infra. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
